messages.subject: Leaf temperature calculations inc a new shiny app
messages.subject_clean: Leaf temperature calculations inc a new shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,
I've recently added functionality to the package for leaf temperature calculations.

There's a new function called 'leaf_temperature' that uses Campbell and Norman's (1998) humid operative temperature approach but solves it with a root finder rather than using their linear approximation.

And the 'ectotherm' function now has a parameter 'leaf' which implements water loss based on stomatal and boundary layer vapour conductance in series (as in the Campbell & Norman model) but with the option to change the shape of the leaf. So if you pass 'leaf = 1' to the model, it will use the new stomatal conductance inputs g_vs_ad and g_vs_ab for the adaxial and abaxial sides of the leaf, which can be a single constant value or an hourly vector that you can modify e.g. as a function of day/night, or soil water potential. If 'leaf=2' then it will open the stomata gradually when leaf temperature rises above the CT_max to maximum values set as 'g_vs_ad_max' and 'g_vs_ab_max'.

The whole setup is also now in the form of a new shiny app <http://bioforecasts.science.unimelb.edu.au/app_direct/leaf_ncep/> which should give you a sense of how it works. Note that in that app by default I've made stomatal openness follow the transpiration predicted by the Soil Plant Atmosphere Continuum model of Campbell's embedded in the microclimate model's soil moisture calcs, and I've provided input options for that part of the model under the microclimate model settings (root properties, critical water potential for stomatal closure, etc.).

I'll explain it all in more detail in a MS that I'm putting together but in the meantime, if you're interested in leaf temperatures, please have a play and let me know if you find any issues with the overall approach and app,  or think of any improvements.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: reserves increasing at the egg stage
messages.subject_clean: reserves increasing at the egg stage
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

Urban Dajčman and I are running some simulations for lizards using DEB and we have realized that something odd is happening at the egg stage. As far as we know, at the egg stage reserves should decrease and structure increases. But apparently reserves increase until hatching, at which point reserves decrease sharply. The same thing happens when we run NicheMapR functions with default parameters. So, we get the attached predictions with this code:

micro <- micro_global(timeinterval = 365)
ecto <- ectotherm(DEB = 1)

We both updated NicheMapR the 5th of July, just in case is related to some recent changes in the code.

Is that supposed to happen?

Thanks a lot in advance!
Urtzi

messages.subject: Re: reserves increasing at the egg stage
messages.subject_clean: reserves increasing at the egg stage
messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

Yes it is - remember that paper we wrote on eggs recently :) They are taking up water and now that water is added to the final wet mass output.
You can check that reserve is not increasing by making this plot of absolute reserve (reserve density (J/cm3) times structural volume (cm3) = total reserve J):
debout <- as.data.frame(ecto$debout)
plot(micro$dates, debout$V * debout$E, type = 'l', ylab = 'reserve, J')
That said, I need to make sure water exchange isn't happening when the reproductive mode is set to viviparous (by default it's oviparous even though the default DEB organism, the water skink, is viviparous).

All the best,
Mike

Essentially, the code is counting the number of instances where that is TRUE but the loop won't run to completion and I'm stuck. I would appreciate your help.

Best regards,
Desire

messages.subject: Re: Error in ectorun(ecto) : NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 4)
messages.subject_clean: Error in ectorun(ecto) : NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 4)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Desire,
What version of the package are you using? Can you also include an example of your code?
Argument 4 is the 'metout' table from the microclimate model, and there must be NA values in it, which was happening in a version of the microclimate model recently after I made some changes for calculating dew. I think I sorted those issues out so you could reinstall the package if you haven't done this in a while via devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR') and see if that fixes it. Also, take a look in metout and see what columns are giving NA values.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject_clean: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
messages.body_plain:
I tried to search in this group and still cant figure it out.
I have a high resolution DEM data of 5m of my study area.
I noticed that the DEM used in the micro_era5 does some interpolations and thus it does not represent my area accuratly.
It is possible to feed the model with my own DEM? If so, how?
Thanks in advance.
Kind Regards,
André Fonseca

messages.subject: Re: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
messages.subject_clean: How to use own terrain data (digital elevation model)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andre,

Yes that's the way to do it. There are two DEM inputs, 'dem' and 'dem2', both used by microclima with the 'dem2' being used for mesoclimatic adjustments (e.g. cold air drainage, coastal effects) and you might want to make 'dem2' lower res if you were using those features (to save compute time). Also note that if you're running lots of simulations on the same sites with different parameters but the same DEM and you are obtaining the DEM automatically via the elevatr package, as occurs by default, it pays to pre-download the DEMs and save them, and then input them as an argument to the micro_era5 call, rather than have the function go to the web all the time.

All the best,
Mike

(do ?microclima::microclimaforNMR for more details).
